patterns.note: A highly structured, almost tabular three-column layout is used for the main project list, presenting Project, Client, and Year in distinct, aligned columns.
A single, clean sans-serif typeface is used consistently across all text elements, including navigation, body text, and project titles, varying only in size and weight.
A stark, monochromatic color scheme of light grey background and dark grey text dominates, allowing project imagery to introduce the only significant color variations.
The top navigation bar dynamically reduces its height and becomes sticky as the user scrolls past the initial hero content, maintaining a compact presence at the top of the viewport.
Project detail pages feature an asymmetric two-column layout, typically with a large image on the left and a concise block of descriptive text and metadata on the right.

technique_notes: The sticky header effect can be rebuilt using CSS position: sticky combined with a JavaScript listener that adds a class to the header element once a specific scroll threshold is met. This class would apply a CSS transition to reduce the header's height and padding, creating a smooth shrinking animation.

The overall minimalist layout relies on a grid system with generous white space, particularly around content blocks and between list items, to create an airy and uncluttered presentation. Project pages utilize a flexible two-column grid for image and text pairings.
Content sections, such as the project list, are presented statically without scroll-triggered reveals or fade-ins, maintaining a direct and immediate display of information.

design_tokens.type_scale: small, consistent sans-serif for body text and navigation, with project titles slightly larger but not dramatically so; headings are generally just larger versions of the body font.
design_tokens.spacing: airy, with significant vertical spacing between project list items and around the hero section, contributing to a clean and uncluttered feel.

standout: This site's design is distinctive for its extreme, almost academic minimalism and highly structured presentation of design work. It eschews typical marketing elements for a direct, content-focused display where the project list itself functions as a primary navigation and content index, presented in a precise, spreadsheet-like format.
